articles.headline: Homestead By The Numbers: Examining The Season Finale Data
articles.dek: A statistical look at the 200-lap championship race at Homestead-Miami Speedway.
articles.body:
The 2028 Cup Series season concluded at Homestead-Miami Speedway with the Straight Talk Wireless 400. Daniel Suarez drove from the pole position to capture his seventh win of the year, leading 70 laps along the way.

Behind the winner, the 36-car field navigated nine caution periods over 200 laps. Strategy and attrition shaped the running order down the stretch, highlighted by Bubba Wallace advancing from a 30th-place start to finish third.

Wallace gained 27 positions by the checkered flag, marking the largest upward movement of any driver in the season finale. Meanwhile, Chase Briscoe secured the championship crown with a second-place finish after starting 14th and pacing the field for 31 laps.

Several contenders failed to reach the finish. Josh Berry, Kyle Larson, Denny Hamlin, and Noah Gragson all fell out of the race due to accidents, ending their campaigns in the garage area.

Suarez crossed the finish line 0.904 seconds ahead of Briscoe to claim the victory. Austin Hill finished fourth after starting 16th and leading 18 laps, while Connor Zilisch rounded out the top five following an 11th-place start and 17 laps led.
articles.author: Priya Nandakumar

articles.headline: Suarez Wins Homestead Finale as Briscoe Clinches Title
articles.dek: Daniel Suarez captured the checkered flag at Homestead-Miami Speedway while Chase Briscoe sealed the championship.
articles.body:
Daniel Suarez drove to victory in the season-ending Straight Talk Wireless 400 at Homestead-Miami Speedway, leading 70 laps on his way to win number seven of the year. Suarez started on the pole and held off a hard-charging field through nine cautions to secure the win by 0.904 seconds.

While Suarez took the race win, Chase Briscoe managed the afternoon safely from the 14th starting spot, leading 31 laps and finishing second to officially claim the season championship with 1281 total points. Briscoe finished the year with 10 wins, cementing a dominant campaign.

The race featured significant movement through the field, highlighted by Bubba Wallace charging from a 30th-place start up to finish third, leading 19 laps along the way. Austin Hill finished fourth after starting 16th and leading 18 laps, while Connor Zilisch rounded out the top five in fifth after climbing from 11th on the grid.

A total of nine caution periods slowed the 200-lap event, collecting several notable contenders. Josh Berry, Kyle Larson, Denny Hamlin, and Noah Gragson all failed to finish after being caught up in on-track accidents.

With the 36-race sim schedule now complete, the NASCAR Cup Series enters the offseason. Teams and drivers will spend the coming weeks reviewing equipment and preparing for the next campaign.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Austin Cindric wins Autotrader 400
articles.dek: Official finish, points and how the championship looks after the race.
articles.body:
Austin Cindric won Autotrader 400 at EchoPark Speedway (Atlanta), starting P28 and leading 66 laps. Brad Keselowski finished second and William Byron was third.

The race ran 188 laps with 7 cautions.

Austin Cindric was the biggest mover, gaining 27 spots from P28 to P1.

Chase Briscoe leads the championship with 1246 points, 99 ahead of Ryan Blaney.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

posts.title: Post-Race Thoughts: Homestead Finale Chaos
posts.text: People are going to talk about Suarez and Briscoe all night, but Bubba Wallace quietly carving his way from P30 to P3 was the drive of the day. Nine cautions meant he had to dodge every single piece of junk on track.
Carving his way through? More like lucking out when half the field wrecked themselves out by lap 150.
Keep making excuses. P30 to P3 with 19 laps led takes actual talent whether you want to admit it or not.
We been knew you'd defend him no matter what. He just stayed out of the way.
1/3 Homestead data breakdown: Daniel Suarez averaged a running position of 1.4 today, completely dominating the front of the field.
Daniel Suarez is the first driver to win from the pole at Homestead since the 2026 season finale.

posts.title: The 2028 Season is in the Books - Final Standings Discussion
posts.text: Looking at the final standings with Briscoe on top at 1281 points and Blaney second at 1161. At least we got a full 36 races of racing, even if the playoff format gives everyone a headache every single year.
Spot on. Byron ending up down in P17 today after starting fifth sums up how weird these final rounds can get when cars start pushing too hard.
Agree completely. Too many cautions at the end ruined what could have been a clean race. - R.
Looking back at the restart strategy in the final stage at Homestead, Austin Hill's crew making that quick adjustment really saved his top five. P4 from sixteenth on the grid is a great recovery.
Ryan Preece grabbing P7 after starting third was a nice steady run too. Got caught up in some battles early but held strong.
too many yellow flags... back in my day they let them RACE instead of bunching them up every ten minutes...
New episode dropping tomorrow morning. We are breaking down every single wreck from Homestead, the championship battle, and why Larson and Hamlin's day ended early. Drop your questions below.
Ask Larson how his rear bumper feels after that lap accident. Brutal end to the year for the 5 team.

chase.headline: Briscoe Leads the Field into the Offseason
chase.summary: Chase Briscoe establishes the benchmark with 1281 points to secure the top spot in the simulated standings. Ryan Blaney follows closely behind with 1161 points, while Daniel Suarez rounds out the top three with 1092 points.

notes.chase briscoe: Secures the highest point total of the field with 1281 points.
notes.ryan blaney: Holds the second position in the standings with 1161 points.
notes.daniel suarez: Claims third in the projections by accumulating 1092 points.
notes.austin cindric: Misses the top tier entirely despite earning 709 points.
notes.tyler reddick: Finishes out the projected order with 572 points.

race.headline: Wrapping Up the Year That Was
race.summary: Drivers put a bow on thirty-six hard-fought events with some wild late-season charges. Suarez closed things out by dominating from the pole, while guys like Briscoe and Hill carved through traffic from deep in the pack.

notes.chase briscoe: Charged forward from a thirty-first starting spot all the way to fifth at Talladega.
notes.ryan blaney: Drove from thirty-sixth to victory lane at the eero 400.
notes.daniel suarez: Controlled the season finale from the pole position and secured the win.
notes.austin hill: Fought his way from twenty-eighth up to a runner-up finish at Martinsville.
notes.brad keselowski: Gained twenty-nine positions after starting thirty-first to finish second at Darlington.

season.headline: The Books Are Closed on Another Campaign
season.summary: Thirty-six races are in the rearview mirror and the final ledger is set in stone. Briscoe stands alone at the summit with 1281 points while the rest of the garage has to wait until next year to catch him.

notes.chase briscoe: Takes home the top spot in the season projections with 1281 points.
notes.ryan blaney: Secures second place in the final rundown with 1161 points.
notes.daniel suarez: Wraps up his campaign in third with 1092 points.
notes.william byron: Climbs from thirty-sixth to finish third at Gateway during the year.
notes.connor zilisch: Puts together a solid late run by marching from twenty-eighth to eighth at the finale.
